title: Putin's Russia
subtitle: Since 1999
subject: comprendreLeMonde
description: In 25 years, a former KGB officer transformed a country in crisis into an authoritarian power. Portrait of **Vladimir Putin** and his regime.

hero.hook: In 1999, almost no one knew his name. Twenty-five years later, he has never left power.

blocks.text: Since his arrival at the top of the state in 1999, **Vladimir Putin** has profoundly transformed Russia. In a quarter of a century, he has transformed a country weakened by the collapse of the USSR into a centralized and bellicose power, which openly defies the international order.

His reign followed a singular trajectory: first perceived as a pragmatic stabilizer, he became the builder of an authoritarian regime, based on the control of energy resources, the repression of all opposition and a nostalgic vision of Russian imperial greatness.

The rise of Vladimir Putin is inseparable from the chaos of the 1990s. A former officer of , the Soviet and then Russian secret services, he cut his teeth in Saint Petersburg before joining President Boris Yeltsin's entourage in Moscow. **[[KGB and FSB]]**
Vladimir Putin was virtually unknown to the general Russian public until August 1999, with 2% popularity. Terrorist attacks and the war in Chechnya propelled it to 80% in a few months.

Elected president in March 2000, he based his mandate on a tacit contract: the return of order and an improvement in the standard of living, in exchange for a gradual abandonment of political freedoms. Driven by soaring oil prices, Russian GDP increased eightfold between 1999 and 2008.

Once stability is achieved, Putin neutralizes all autonomous centers of power. He begins by domesticating the **[[oligarch]]**, these businessmen enriched during the chaotic privatizations of the Yeltsin era. The signal was given in 2003 with the arrest of Mikhail Khodorkovsky, boss of a large oil company.

The regime also attacks press freedom: television channels come under the control of public companies like Gazprom, transforming information into propaganda. The opponent Alexeï Navalny embodies the internal challenge: after a poisoning in 2020, he was imprisoned upon his return, and died in a penal colony in February 2024.
Although his official salary is modest, Vladimir Putin is often seen with luxury watches whose value far exceeds his declared income.

The very structure of the State is evolving towards a system dominated by the **[[siloviki]]**, representatives of force structures such as the army or the secret services. They occupy key positions in the administration and large public companies, merging security and financial interests around the Putin clan.

sections.title: Towards the break with the West

blocks.text: Putin's geopolitical vision is based on a trauma: the disappearance of the USSR, which he describes as "the greatest geopolitical catastrophe of the 20th century". Its foreign policy aims to restore a zone of influence around Russia, by opposing NATO expansion, seen as aggression.

The escalation takes the form of the use of force: in 2008 in Georgia, then in 2014 when Russia illegally annexes Crimea and supports an armed insurrection in eastern Ukraine, the Donbass. These acts mark the return of the territorial war in Europe.

blocks.caption: Vladimir Putin has led Russia since 1999, first as president, then as prime minister, then as president again.

blocks.text: The total invasion of Ukraine, launched on February 24, 2022, pushes Russia into a total break with the West. It triggers the most massive economic sanctions in modern history, and paradoxically strengthens European and transatlantic unity in the face of the Russian threat.

sections.title: The ideology of the regime and the perpetuation of power

blocks.text: To legitimize this confrontation, the Kremlin is developing a doctrine called : a specific Russian path, based on conservative values, in opposition to a West considered decadent. The regime rewrites history, glorifying the 1945 victory and downplaying Stalinist crimes. [[“Sovereign democracy”]]

Putin locked his stay in power through a constitutional reform in 2020, which theoretically allows him to remain president until 2036, while laws on “foreign agents” serve to liquidate the last organizations of **civil society**.

Putin came to power in 1999 promising stability. In twenty-five years, he rebuilt a strong state, muzzled the opposition and transformed Russia into a belligerent authoritarian regime, engaged in a violent challenge to the world order.
